sanskrit: evaṃ ye jñātayo 'rtheṣu mitho gacchanti vigraham te 'mitravaśam āyānti śakunāv iva vigrahāt
english: Likewise, those kinsmen who fall into mutual strife over wealth come under the power of their enemies, just as the two birds did through their quarrel.

sanskrit: saṃbhojanaṃ saṃkathanaṃ saṃpraśno 'tha samāgamaḥ etāni jñātikāryāṇi na virodhaḥ kadā cana
english: Eating together, conversing together, asking after one another, and meeting together — these are the duties of kinsmen; never is strife among them proper.

sanskrit: yasmin kāle sumanasaḥ sarve vṛddhān upāsate siṃhaguptam ivāraṇyam apradhṛṣyā bhavanti te
english: In that age when all men of good will serve and honour their elders, they become invincible, like a forest protected by a lion.

sanskrit: ye 'rthaṃ saṃtatam āsādya dīnā iva samāsate śriyaṃ te saṃprayacchanti dviṣadbhyo bharatarṣabha
english: Those who, having obtained wealth, sit dejected and despondent, hand over their prosperity to their enemies, O bull of the Bhārata line.

sanskrit: dhūmāyante vyapetāni jvalanti sahitāni ca dhṛtarāṣṭrolmukānīva jñātayo bharatarṣabha
english: Kinsmen separated from each other smoulder like firebrands of Dhṛtarāṣṭra; united, they blaze brightly, O bull of the Bhāratas.

sanskrit: idam anyat pravakṣyāmi yathā dṛṣṭaṃ girau mayā śrutvā tad api kauravya yathā śreyas tathā kuru
english: I will now tell you something else that I myself witnessed on a mountain. Hear it too, O Kauravya, and act for your own good accordingly.

sanskrit: vayaṃ kirātaiḥ sahitā gacchāmo girim uttaram brāhmaṇair devakalpaiś ca vidyājambhakavātikaiḥ
english: We were travelling together with Kirātas and with Brahmins equal to the gods — those skilled in the lore of the Jambhaka and Vatika sciences — towards the northern mountain.

sanskrit: kuñjabhūtaṃ giriṃ sarvam abhito gandhamādanam dīpyamānauṣadhigaṇaṃ siddhagandharvasevitam
english: The whole of Gandhamādana mountain was densely forested, its masses of herbs glowing with light, and it was frequented by Siddhas and Gandharvas.

sanskrit: tatra paśyāmahe sarve madhu pītam amākṣikam maruprapāte viṣame niviṣṭaṃ kumbhasaṃmitam
english: There we all saw honey, pale and free of bees, stored in a jar-sized deposit, lodged in a difficult desert ravine.

sanskrit: āśīviṣai rakṣyamāṇaṃ kuberadayitaṃ bhṛśam yat prāśya puruṣo martyo amaratvaṃ nigacchati
english: It was guarded by venomous serpents and was exceedingly dear to Kubera; a mortal man who tasted it would attain immortality.

sanskrit: acakṣur labhate cakṣur vṛddho bhavati vai yuvā iti te kathayanti sma brāhmaṇā jambhasādhakāḥ
english: "The sightless gain sight; the old become young again" — so declared those Brahmins who were adepts in the Jambhaka science.

sanskrit: tataḥ kirātās tad dṛṣṭvā prārthayanto mahīpate vineśur viṣame tasmin sasarpe girigahvare
english: Then the Kirātas, O king, beholding it and coveting it, perished in that treacherous mountain cave infested with serpents.

sanskrit: tathaiva tava putro 'yaṃ pṛthivīm eka icchati madhu paśyati saṃmohāt prapātaṃ nānupaśyati
english: In just the same way, your son desires to possess the whole earth alone; blinded by delusion, he sees the honey but does not see the precipice.

sanskrit: duryodhano yoddhumanāḥ samare savyasācinā na ca paśyāmi tejo 'sya vikramaṃ vā tathāvidham
english: Duryodhana is eager to fight Savyasācin in battle, yet I do not see in him such splendour or valour as would match that.

sanskrit: ekena ratham āsthāya pṛthivī yena nirjitā pratīkṣamāṇo yo vīraḥ kṣamate vīkṣitaṃ tava
english: That hero who conquered the entire earth single-handedly from his chariot stands waiting, bearing your gaze with patience, O king.

sanskrit: drupado matsyarājaś ca saṃkruddhaś ca dhanaṃjayaḥ na śeṣayeyuḥ samare vāyuyuktā ivāgnayaḥ
english: Drupada, the king of the Matsyas, and the enraged Dhanañjaya — like fires fanned by the wind, they would leave no remnant on the battlefield.

sanskrit: aṅke kuruṣva rājānaṃ dhṛtarāṣṭra yudhiṣṭhiram yudhyator hi dvayor yuddhe naikāntena bhavej jayaḥ
english: Take king Yudhiṣṭhira to your heart, O Dhṛtarāṣṭra; for when two such warriors fight, victory cannot be certain for either side.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca duryodhana vijānīhi yat tvāṃ vakṣyāmi putraka utpathaṃ manyase mārgam anabhijña ivādhvagaḥ
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: Duryodhana, understand what I am about to say to you, my son. You think a wrong path is the right road, like a traveller who has lost his way.

sanskrit: pañcānāṃ pāṇḍuputrāṇāṃ yat tejaḥ pramimīṣasi pañcānām iva bhūtānāṃ mahatāṃ sumahātmanām
english: You presume to measure the splendour of the five sons of Pāṇḍu as if measuring the five great elements — those souls of surpassing greatness.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhiraṃ hi kaunteyaṃ paraṃ dharmam ihāsthitam parāṃ gatim asaṃprekṣya na tvaṃ vettum ihārhasi
english: As for Yudhiṣṭhira, the son of Kuntī, who is established in the highest Dharma here — you are not capable of knowing him without perceiving his ultimate station.

sanskrit: bhīmasenaṃ ca kaunteyaṃ yasya nāsti samo bale raṇāntakaṃ tarkayase mahāvātam iva drumaḥ
english: And Bhīmasena, the son of Kuntī, who has no equal in strength — you reckon him, the ender of battles, as a tree might reckon a great storm.

sanskrit: sarvaśastrabhṛtāṃ śreṣṭhaṃ meruṃ śikhariṇām iva yudhi gāṇḍīvadhanvānaṃ ko nu yudhyeta buddhimān
english: The wielder of Gāṇḍīva's bow, foremost among all bearers of weapons, like Mount Meru among mountains — what wise man would fight him in battle?

sanskrit: dhṛṣṭadyumnaś ca pāñcālyaḥ kam ivādya na śātayet śatrumadhye śarān muñcan devarāḍ aśanīm iva
english: And Dhṛṣṭadyumna of the Pāñcālas — like Indra hurling his thunderbolt, loosing arrows into the midst of enemies, whom today would he not strike down?

sanskrit: sātyakiś cāpi durdharṣaḥ saṃmato 'ndhakavṛṣṇiṣu dhvaṃsayiṣyati te senāṃ pāṇḍaveyahite rataḥ
english: And Sātyaki too, fierce and invincible, honoured among the Andhakas and Vṛṣṇis, devoted to the welfare of the Pāṇḍava line, will shatter your army.

sanskrit: yaḥ punaḥ pratimānena trīṃl lokān atiricyate taṃ kṛṣṇaṃ puṇḍarīkākṣaḥ ko nu yudhyeta buddhimān
english: And that Kṛṣṇa of the lotus eyes who surpasses the three worlds in glory — what wise man would fight him?

sanskrit: ekato hy asya dārāś ca jñātayaś ca sabāndhavāḥ ātmā ca pṛthivī ceyam ekataś ca dhanaṃjayaḥ
english: On one side are his wives, his kinsmen, and his relations, and this whole earth itself; on the other side stands Dhanañjaya alone — and he values them equally.

sanskrit: vāsudevo 'pi durdharṣo yatātmā yatra pāṇḍavaḥ aviṣahyaṃ pṛthivyāpi tad balaṃ yatra keśavaḥ
english: Vāsudeva too is fierce and self-controlled; wherever the Pāṇḍava stands, that force is unbearable even for the earth — for Keśava is there.

sanskrit: tiṣṭha tāta satāṃ vākye suhṛdām arthavādinām vṛddhaṃ śāṃtanavaṃ bhīṣmaṃ titikṣasva pitāmaham
english: Abide, my son, by the counsel of the virtuous and of friends who speak for your benefit. Endure with patience your grandsire Bhīṣma, the son of Śaṃtanu.

sanskrit: māṃ ca bruvāṇaṃ śuśrūṣa kurūṇām arthavādinam droṇaṃ kṛpaṃ vikarṇaṃ ca mahārājaṃ ca bāhlikam
english: And heed me as I counsel you for the good of the Kurus. Listen also to Droṇa, Kṛpa, Vikarṇa, and the great king Bāhlika.

sanskrit: ete hy api yathaivāhaṃ mantum arhasi tāṃs tathā sarve dharmavido hy ete tulyasnehāś ca bhārata
english: These men you should regard just as you regard me, O Bhārata; for all of them are versed in Dharma and bear equal affection for you.

sanskrit: yat tad virāṭanagare saha bhrātṛbhir agrataḥ utsṛjya gāḥ susaṃtrastaṃ balaṃ te samaśīryata
english: What happened in the city of Virāṭa, when your army, panic-stricken, abandoned the cattle and scattered before Arjuna and his brothers —

sanskrit: yac caiva tasmin nagare śrūyate mahad adbhutam ekasya ca bahūnāṃ ca paryāptaṃ tan nidarśanam
english: — and what extraordinary and wondrous things are heard to have occurred in that city, wrought by one against many — that example alone should suffice you.

sanskrit: arjunas tat tathākārṣīt kiṃ punaḥ sarva eva te sabhrātṝn abhijānīhi vṛttyā ca pratipādaya
english: If Arjuna alone accomplished all that, what more need be said when all of them act together? Acknowledge your brothers and provide for them according to their due.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca evam uktvā mahāprājño dhṛtarāṣṭraḥ suyodhanam punar eva mahābhāgaḥ saṃjayaṃ paryapṛcchata
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Having spoken thus to Suyodhana, the greatly wise and illustrious Dhṛtarāṣṭra turned again to question Sañjaya.

sanskrit: brūhi saṃjaya yac cheṣaṃ vāsudevād anantaram yad arjuna uvāca tvāṃ paraṃ kautūhalaṃ hi me
english: "Tell me, Sañjaya, what remained after Vāsudeva had spoken — what Arjuna said to you; I am greatly eager to hear it."

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca vāsudevavacaḥ śrutvā kuntīputro dhanaṃjayaḥ uvāca kāle durdharṣo vāsudevasya śṛṇvataḥ
english: Sañjaya said: Having heard the words of Vāsudeva, Dhanañjaya, the son of Kuntī — fierce and unyielding — spoke in due course while Vāsudeva listened.

sanskrit: pitāmahaṃ śāṃtanavaṃ dhṛtarāṣṭraṃ ca saṃjaya droṇaṃ kṛpaṃ ca karṇaṃ ca mahārājaṃ ca bāhlikam
english: "Bhīṣma the son of Śaṃtanu, Dhṛtarāṣṭra, O Sañjaya, Droṇa, Kṛpa, Karṇa, and the great king Bāhlika —

sanskrit: drauṇiṃ ca somadattaṃ ca śakuniṃ cāpi saubalam duḥśāsanaṃ śalaṃ caiva purumitraṃ viviṃśatim
english: — Aśvatthāmā, Somadatta, Śakuni the son of Subala, Duḥśāsana, Śala, Purumitra, and Viviṃśati —

sanskrit: vikarṇaṃ citrasenaṃ ca jayatsenaṃ ca pārthivam vindānuvindāv āvantyau durmukhaṃ cāpi kauravam
english: — Vikarṇa, Citrasena, King Jayadratha, Vinda and Anuvinda from the Avantis, and Durmukha of the Kuru line —

sanskrit: saindhavaṃ duḥsahaṃ caiva bhūriśravasam eva ca bhagadattaṃ ca rājānaṃ jalasaṃdhaṃ ca pārthivam
english: — the Sindhu king, Duhsaha, Bhūriśravas, King Bhagadatta, and the king Jalanandha —

sanskrit: ye cāpy anye pārthivās tatra yoddhuṃ; samāgatāḥ kauravāṇāṃ priyārtham mumūrṣavaḥ pāṇḍavāgnau pradīpte; samānītā dhārtarāṣṭreṇa sūta
english: — and whatever other kings have assembled there to fight for the good of the Kauravas, ready to die in the fire of the Pāṇḍavas when it blazes up, gathered there by Dhṛtarāṣṭra's son, O charioteer —

sanskrit: yathānyāyaṃ kauśalaṃ vandanaṃ ca; samāgatā madvacanena vācyāḥ idaṃ brūyāḥ saṃjaya rājamadhye; suyodhanaṃ pāpakṛtāṃ pradhānam
english: — all these assembled men are to be greeted with proper courtesy and salutation on my behalf; say this, Sañjaya, in the midst of that assembly: to Suyodhana, the foremost of evil-doers —

sanskrit: amarṣaṇaṃ durmatiṃ rājaputraṃ; pāpātmānaṃ dhārtarāṣṭraṃ sulubdham sarvaṃ mamaitad vacanaṃ samagraṃ; sahāmātyaṃ saṃjaya śrāvayethāḥ
english: — that wrathful, evil-minded prince, that wicked and utterly greedy son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra — let him together with his counsellors hear this entire message of mine, O Sañjaya.

sanskrit: evaṃ pratiṣṭhāpya dhanaṃjayo māṃ; tato 'rthavad dharmavac cāpi vākyam provācedaṃ vāsudevaṃ samīkṣya; pārtho dhīmāṃl lohitāntāyatākṣaḥ
english: Having thus established his charge to me, Dhanañjaya then turned to look at Vāsudeva and spoke this further word, purposeful and righteous — Pṛthā's son, the wise one, his wide eyes red at their corners.

sanskrit: yathā śrutaṃ te vadato mahātmano; madhupravīrasya vacaḥ samāhitam tathaiva vācyaṃ bhavatā hi madvacaḥ; samāgateṣu kṣitipeṣu sarvaśaḥ
english: "As you have heard the collected words of that great-souled hero Madhupravira spoken, so too shall my words be delivered by you, to all the assembled kings, everywhere."

sanskrit: śarāgnidhūme rathaneminādite; dhanuḥsruveṇāstrabalāpahāriṇā yathā na homaḥ kriyate mahāmṛdhe; tathā sametya prayatadhvam ādṛtāḥ
english: "As no sacrificial oblation is performed amid the smoke of arrow-fire and the din of chariot-wheels, with the bow as ladle and the power of weapons as the oblation — so, having come together, strive with care and reverence before that great battle begins."

sanskrit: na cet prayacchadhvam amitraghātino; yudhiṣṭhirasyāṃśam abhīpsitaṃ svakam nayāmi vaḥ svāśvapadātikuñjarān; diśaṃ pitṝṇām aśivāṃ śitaiḥ śaraiḥ
english: "If you will not yield to the slayer of foes the share of Yudhiṣṭhira that is rightfully desired, then with sharp arrows I shall send your horses, foot-soldiers, and elephants to the inauspicious realm of the ancestors."

sanskrit: tato 'ham āmantrya caturbhujaṃ hariṃ; dhanaṃjayaṃ caiva namasya satvaraḥ javena saṃprāpta ihāmaradyute; tavāntikaṃ prāpayituṃ vaco mahat
english: Then, having taken leave of four-armed Hari and bowing to Dhanañjaya, I swiftly departed and came here with speed, O you of divine radiance, to bring this momentous message to your presence.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca duryodhane dhārtarāṣṭre tad vaco 'pratinandati tūṣṇīṃbhūteṣu sarveṣu samuttasthur nareśvarāḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: When Duryodhana, the son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, did not welcome that speech and all fell silent, the assembled kings rose from their seats.

sanskrit: utthiteṣu mahārāja pṛthivyāṃ sarvarājasu rahite saṃjayaṃ rājā paripraṣṭuṃ pracakrame
english: O great king, when all the kings of the earth had risen and departed and they were alone, the king proceeded to question Sañjaya.

sanskrit: āśaṃsamāno vijayaṃ teṣāṃ putravaśānugaḥ ātmanaś ca pareṣāṃ ca pāṇḍavānāṃ ca niścayam
english: Led by submission to his son's will, yet hoping for their victory, he sought to know the resolve of both sides — his own and the Pāṇḍavas'.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca gāvalgaṇe brūhi naḥ sāraphalgu; svasenāyāṃ yāvad ihāsti kiṃ cit tvaṃ pāṇḍavānāṃ nipuṇaṃ vettha sarvaṃ; kim eṣāṃ jyāyaḥ kim u teṣāṃ kanīyaḥ
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: Son of Gavalgaṇa, tell us what is substance and what is dross — whatever exists in our own army — for you know everything about the Pāṇḍavas with precision. What is greater on their side, what is lesser on ours?

sanskrit: tvam etayoḥ sāravit sarvadarśī; dharmārthayor nipuṇo niścayajñaḥ sa me pṛṣṭaḥ saṃjaya brūhi sarvaṃ; yudhyamānāḥ katare 'smin na santi
english: You are the one who knows the essence of both sides and sees all; you are skilled in Dharma and wealth, knowing the certain truth. Thus questioned by me, O Sañjaya, tell all — which of those who would fight will not survive this?

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca na tvāṃ brūyāṃ rahite jātu kiṃ cid; asūyā hi tvāṃ prasaheta rājan ānayasva pitaraṃ saṃśitavrataṃ; gāṃdhārīṃ ca mahiṣīm ājamīḍha
english: Sañjaya said: I would never tell you anything in private, O king, for envy would overpower you. Bring your father, firm in his vows, and Queen Gāndhārī, O descendant of Ajamīḍha.

sanskrit: tau te 'sūyāṃ vinayetāṃ narendra; dharmajñau tau nipuṇau niścayajñau tayos tu tvāṃ saṃnidhau tad vadeyaṃ; kṛtsnaṃ mataṃ vāsudevārjunābhyām
english: Those two would curb your envy, O lord of men; both are knowers of Dharma, both skilled and sure in judgment. In their presence I would tell you in full the entire counsel of Vāsudeva and Arjuna.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tatas tan matam ājñāya saṃjayasyātmajasya ca abhyupetya mahāprājñaḥ kṛṣṇadvaipāyano 'bravīt
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Then, having understood the mind of Sañjaya and of his own son, the greatly wise Kṛṣṇa Dvaipāyana came forward and spoke.

sanskrit: saṃpṛcchate dhṛtarāṣṭrāya saṃjaya; ācakṣva sarvaṃ yāvad eṣo 'nuyuṅkte sarvaṃ yāvad vettha tasmin yathāvad; yāthātathyaṃ vāsudeve 'rjune ca
english: "Sañjaya, to Dhṛtarāṣṭra who asks you, declare everything as far as he inquires; declare everything you truly know about the matter, exactly as it stands — the truth regarding Vāsudeva and Arjuna."

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca arjuno vāsudevaś ca dhanvinau paramārcitau kāmād anyatra saṃbhūtau sarvābhāvāya saṃmitau
english: Sañjaya said: Arjuna and Vāsudeva — two supreme archers, supremely honoured, arisen beyond desire, balanced toward the welfare of all beings —

sanskrit: dyām antaraṃ samāsthāya yathāyuktaṃ manasvinaḥ cakraṃ tad vāsudevasya māyayā vartate vibho
english: — dwelling in the space between heaven and earth as is befitting to those great souls, Vāsudeva's wheel turns there by his maya, O lord.

sanskrit: sāpahnavaṃ pāṇḍaveṣu pāṇḍavānāṃ susaṃmatam sārāsārabalaṃ jñātvā tat samāsena me śṛṇu
english: Having known the strength and weakness of the force that is adverse to the Pāṇḍavas yet highly esteemed among the Pāṇḍavas themselves, hear it from me in brief.

sanskrit: narakaṃ śambaraṃ caiva kaṃsaṃ caidyaṃ ca mādhavaḥ jitavān ghorasaṃkāśān krīḍann iva janārdanaḥ
english: Naraka, Śambara, Kaṃsa, and the Cedi king — all of terrible aspect — Mādhava, Janārdana, conquered them as if in sport.

sanskrit: pṛthivīṃ cāntarikṣaṃ ca dyāṃ caiva puruṣottamaḥ manasaiva viśiṣṭātmā nayaty ātmavaśaṃ vaśī
english: The earth, the sky, and the heavens — the Uttama Puruṣa, that supremely distinguished soul, the self-controlled one, brings them all under his own will by mind alone.

sanskrit: bhūyo bhūyo hi yad rājan pṛcchase pāṇḍavān prati sārāsārabalaṃ jñātuṃ tan me nigadataḥ śṛṇu
english: Since you keep asking again and again, O king, in order to know the strength and weakness of the Pāṇḍava force, hear it from me as I speak.

sanskrit: ekato vā jagat kṛtsnam ekato vā janārdanaḥ sārato jagataḥ kṛtsnād atirikto janārdanaḥ
english: On one side the whole universe; on the other Janārdana — Janārdana surpasses the entire universe in essence.

sanskrit: bhasma kuryāj jagad idaṃ manasaiva janārdanaḥ na tu kṛtsnaṃ jagac chaktaṃ bhasma kartuṃ janārdanam
english: Janārdana could reduce this universe to ash by mind alone; but the entire universe is not capable of reducing Janārdana to ash.

sanskrit: yataḥ satyaṃ yato dharmo yato hrīr ārjavaṃ yataḥ tato bhavati govindo yataḥ kṛṣṇas tato jayaḥ
english: Where truth is, where Dharma is, where modesty and uprightness are — there Govinda abides. Where Kṛṣṇa is, there is victory.

sanskrit: pṛthivīṃ cāntarikṣaṃ ca divaṃ ca puruṣottamaḥ viceṣṭayati bhūtātmā krīḍann iva janārdanaḥ
english: The Uttama Puruṣa, the soul of all beings, Janārdana, stirs earth, sky, and heaven as if in sport.

sanskrit: sa kṛtvā pāṇḍavān satraṃ lokaṃ saṃmohayann iva adharmaniratān mūḍhān dagdhum icchati te sutān
english: Making the Pāṇḍavas his sacrificial session and bewitching the world, as it were, he desires to burn your sons — those fools devoted to unrighteousness.

sanskrit: kālacakraṃ jagaccakraṃ yugacakraṃ ca keśavaḥ ātmayogena bhagavān parivartayate 'niśam
english: Keśava, the Bhagavān, turns the wheel of time, the wheel of the world, and the wheel of the ages without ceasing by means of his own yoga.

sanskrit: kālasya ca hi mṛtyoś ca jaṅgamasthāvarasya ca īśate bhagavān ekaḥ satyam etad bravīmi te
english: Of time, of death, and of all that moves and stands still, the Bhagavān alone is the lord — this is the truth I declare to you.

sanskrit: īśann api mahāyogī sarvasya jagato hariḥ karmāṇy ārabhate kartuṃ kīnāśa iva durbalaḥ
english: Even though Hari, the great Yogin, is lord of the entire universe, he undertakes actions to perform them as if he were a weak labourer.

sanskrit: tena vañcayate lokān māyāyogena keśavaḥ ye tam eva prapadyante na te muhyanti mānavāḥ
english: By that means Keśava bewilders the worlds through his yoga of maya; but those mortals who surrender to him alone are not deluded.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca kathaṃ tvaṃ mādhavaṃ vettha sarvalokamaheśvaram katham enaṃ na vedāhaṃ tan mamācakṣva saṃjaya
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: How is it that you know Mādhava as the great lord of all worlds, while I do not know him so? Tell me this, Sañjaya.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca vidyā rājan na te vidyā mama vidyā na hīyate vidyāhīnas tamodhvasto nābhijānāti keśavam
english: Sañjaya said: Knowledge, O king — you do not have it; my knowledge is not diminished. One devoid of knowledge, overwhelmed by darkness, does not recognise Keśava.

sanskrit: vidyayā tāta jānāmi triyugaṃ madhusūdanam kartāram akṛtaṃ devaṃ bhūtānāṃ prabhavāpyayam
english: By knowledge, dear one, I know Madhusūdana as he who pervades the three ages — the uncreated maker, the god who is the origin and dissolution of all beings.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca gāvalgaṇe 'tra kā bhaktir yā te nityā janārdane yayā tvam abhijānāsi triyugaṃ madhusūdanam
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: Son of Gavalgaṇa, what devotion is it that you have constantly toward Janārdana, by which you know Madhusūdana as pervading the three ages?

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca māyāṃ na seve bhadraṃ te na vṛthādharmam ācare śuddhabhāvaṃ gato bhaktyā śāstrād vedmi janārdanam
english: Sañjaya said: I do not resort to illusion — may it go well with you; I do not practise unrighteous conduct in vain. With a purified heart, through devotion and through scripture, I know Janārdana.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca duryodhana hṛṣīkeśaṃ prapadyasva janārdanam āpto naḥ saṃjayas tāta śaraṇaṃ gaccha keśavam
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: Duryodhana, surrender to Hṛṣīkeśa, to Janārdana. Our trusted Sañjaya has spoken — dear son, seek refuge in Keśava.

sanskrit: duryodhana uvāca bhagavān devakīputro lokaṃ cen nihaniṣyati pravadann arjune sakhyaṃ nāhaṃ gacche 'dya keśavam
english: Duryodhana said: If the Bhagavān, the son of Devakī, will destroy the world while proclaiming his friendship for Arjuna, I will not go to Keśava today.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca avāg gāndhāri putrās te gacchaty eṣa sudurmatiḥ īrṣyur durātmā mānī ca śreyasāṃ vacanātigaḥ
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: Downward goes this son of yours and Gāndhārī — this man of utterly wicked mind, envious, evil-souled, arrogant, and a transgressor of the counsel of his betters.
